council_tax_band_a.label: Average Band A Council Tax, England (£ per year)
council_tax_band_a.publisher: MHCLG (DLUHC) – Council Tax levels set by local authorities in England
council_tax_band_a.methodology: Average Band D for the area, including parish precepts and the adult social care precept. Key = year the financial year starts (2025 = 2025-26). 2002-2011 are from the frozen 2011-12 release (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5a796f41ed915d042206863f/1870223.xls); 2012 onward refreshed from the latest release. Band A = Band D x 6/9, the fixed statutory ratio for England (applies equally to every authority).
council_tax_band_a.limitations: England only (Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have different systems). Band D is a reference band, not what the typical household pays: most English homes are in Bands A-C, so the average bill is lower. 1993-2001 not integrated. Council Tax benefit/reduction is not modelled. Derived arithmetically, not separately published as an England average.

cpi_actual_rents.label: CPI: actual rents for housing index (2015=100)
cpi_actual_rents.source_title: CPI INDEX 04.1 : ACTUAL RENTS FOR HOUSING 2015=100
cpi_actual_rents.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpi_actual_rents.methodology: Price index of rents paid by tenants (private and social), annual figure as published by ONS.
cpi_actual_rents.limitations: An index of rent inflation, not average rents in pounds. Includes social rents. £ average private rents exist only from the 2010s (ONS PIPR) and are not integrated.

cpi_electricity_gas.label: CPI: electricity, gas and other fuels index (2015=100)
cpi_electricity_gas.source_title: CPI INDEX 04.5 : ELECTRICITY, GAS AND OTHER FUELS 2015=100
cpi_electricity_gas.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpi_electricity_gas.methodology: Price index for household electricity, gas and other fuels (not a bill in £).
cpi_electricity_gas.limitations: An index, not a £ bill. Use with a base-year bill to estimate cost changes.

cpi_index.label: CPI all items index (2015=100)
cpi_index.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpi_index.methodology: Consumer Prices Index, annual figure as published by ONS.
cpi_index.limitations: Index from 1988. CPI excludes owner-occupier housing costs.

cpi_motor_insurance.label: CPI: motor vehicle insurance index (2015=100)
cpi_motor_insurance.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpi_motor_insurance.limitations: Index, not £ premiums; may start after 1990.

cpi_new_cars.label: CPI: new cars index (2015=100)
cpi_new_cars.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpi_new_cars.limitations: Quality-adjusted index, not average transaction prices in £.

cpi_rail_fares.label: CPI: passenger transport by railway index (2015=100)
cpi_rail_fares.source_title: CPI INDEX 07.3.1 : PASSENGER TRANSPORT BY RAILWAY 2015=100
cpi_rail_fares.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)

cpi_rate.label: CPI annual inflation rate
cpi_rate.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)

cpih_index.label: CPIH all items index (2015=100)
cpih_index.adjustment: Original (not seasonally adjusted unless stated in title)
cpih_index.methodology: CPI including owner occupiers' housing costs.

earnings_boe_composite.label: Composite average weekly earnings (£/week), Bank of England historical dataset
earnings_boe_composite.publisher: Bank of England (compiled from ONS and earlier official sources)
earnings_boe_composite.methodology: Composite earnings series spliced by the BoE from official sources.
earnings_boe_composite.limitations: Ends 2016. Definition differs from ONS AWE (2000 onward): the two overlap in 2000-2016 and differ by a few percent; do not treat the splice as one survey.

earnings_median_ft.label: Median gross weekly earnings, full-time adults, UK (ASHE)
earnings_median_ft.source_id: UK Median Time-series, Male & Female Adult 50th percentile
earnings_median_ft.methodology: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings, adults on adult rates whose pay was not affected by absence. Years shown as 2004inc/2006inc are used (the series comparable with later years).
earnings_median_ft.limitations: Full-time employees only (excludes part-time and self-employed). Survey changes from 2023 mean 2022-23 comparisons need caution; latest year is provisional.

earnings_median_ft_nes.label: Median gross weekly earnings, full-time adults, GB (New Earnings Survey, 1990-96)
earnings_median_ft_nes.source_id: GB Median Time-series, Male & Female Adult 50th percentile
earnings_median_ft_nes.methodology: New Earnings Survey, the predecessor of ASHE. Great Britain, not UK.
earnings_median_ft_nes.limitations: Different survey and geography from ASHE (1997 onward): do not treat as one continuous series without noting the break.

energy_elec_direct_debit.label: Average annual electricity bill, direct debit, UK (£/year)
energy_elec_direct_debit.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

uk_tax_rules.scope: England, Wales and Northern Ireland; single person under 65; employee, not contracted out
uk_tax_rules.limitations: Scottish income tax bands differ from 2017-18. Ignores pension contributions, student loan, tax credits, benefits in kind and Class 1 contracting-out. 2022-23 and 2023-24 NI are time-weighted across in-year rate changes.

gaps.title: Earnings distribution beyond the median
gaps.detail: Median full-time pay is now integrated (ASHE UK 1997 on, NES GB 1990-96 as a separate line; percentiles stored). Not integrated: part-time and self-employed pay, earnings by decile in the dashboard, and a continuous median across the 1996/97 survey change.

gaps.title: Earnings series break at 2000
gaps.detail: 1990-1999 uses the Bank of England composite average weekly earnings; 2000 onward uses ONS AWE (whole economy, total pay). The two overlap 2000-2016 and differ by a few percent. The dashboard flags years that use the earlier series.

gaps.title: Household disposable income
gaps.detail: ONS household disposable income per head is not yet integrated; take-home pay is computed for a single employee from HMRC tax rules, excluding benefits, tax credits, pension contributions and student loans.

gaps.title: Average private rent in £
gaps.detail: ONS CPI actual-rents index (2015=100, 1988 on) is integrated as a rent-inflation measure and includes social rents. Average private rents in pounds (ONS PIPR/VOA) exist only from the 2010s and are not integrated; no rent figure in £ is shown or estimated for earlier years.

gaps.title: Council Tax: England before 2002 and Northern Ireland
gaps.detail: England Band D 2002-2026, Scotland 1996-2026 and Wales 1993-2026 are integrated, with Bands A-H (Wales A-I) derived from the published average Band D using the statutory ratios in force each year. Not integrated: England 1993-2001; Northern Ireland, which has no Council Tax (domestic rates are charged on each property's capital value, no band system or comparable average-bill series found); Scottish water/waste-water charges; Council Tax reduction; the typical (not Band D) bill. Nations' Band D figures are on slightly different bases (England and Wales include parish/community and, for Wales, police elements) so compare levels with care.

gaps.title: Mortgage rates 1990-1994
gaps.detail: 1990-1994 uses the building societies' basic mortgage rate (ONS AJNK via the Bank of England historical dataset); 1995 onward uses the Bank of England quoted household rate. The two agree within 0.03pp in the 1995 overlap.

gaps.title: Deposit requirements and first-time-buyer data
gaps.detail: Typical deposit/loan-to-value by year is not integrated. The calculator uses a user-set deposit percentage (an assumption, not an observation).

gaps.title: RPI average-price series end in 2024 or earlier
gaps.detail: ONS RPI average prices stop at 2024 for most items, 2023 for pork, 2021 for eggs (size 4) and 2012 for butter. 2025-26 comparisons use the latest observation only if you switch that option on, and the page labels it.

gaps.title: Rice, pasta and several staples
gaps.detail: No continuous ONS average-price series for rice or pasta was found. They are listed as unavailable, not estimated.

gaps.title: Energy bills in £ before 2010
gaps.detail: DESNZ publishes £ bills from 2010 in the tables used here. For earlier years the dashboard can show only the ONS CPI electricity/gas/other-fuels index, clearly marked as an index-scaled estimate, not an observed bill.

gaps.title: Five vehicle categories (small, family, mid-range, van, luxury)
gaps.detail: No benchmark vehicle prices, insurance premiums in £, MOT, servicing, tyres or VED rates are integrated. Only the ONS quality-adjusted new-car and motor-insurance price indices, rail-fare index and petrol/diesel pump prices are available.

gaps.title: VED, Corporation Tax, Stamp Duty and other rate histories
gaps.detail: Integrated: fuel duty (HMRC dated history, day-weighted per year) and VAT (standard rate and domestic fuel rate; hand-curated from legislation.gov.uk and a secondary compilation, the April 1994 domestic-fuel start day is assumed). Not integrated: Vehicle Excise Duty history (needs parsing of VERA 1994 Schedule 1 versions; CO2-band regimes from 2001 and 2017), Corporation Tax, Stamp Duty, alcohol and tobacco duties, and VAT on spending other than petrol and household energy.

gaps.title: Complete receipts breakdown
gaps.detail: PAYE income tax receipts start in 1993 in the ONS series used; total income tax, corporation tax receipts and total public-sector receipts are not yet integrated. Components overlap and must not be summed.

gaps.title: Company financials: only six 20-F filers, 2017 onward
gaps.detail: BP, Shell, Barclays, HSBC, NatWest and Lloyds are loaded from SEC EDGAR (group, statutory IFRS, XBRL era about 2017 onward; some items untagged for some years, e.g. HSBC profit attributable 2023+). Not integrated: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Morrisons, Centrica/EDF and food producers (no 20-F; need annual-report extraction), all pre-2017 years, UK-only segment results, adjusted/underlying profit. Group results must not be read as UK results.

gaps.title: Regional earnings
gaps.detail: Regional house prices are integrated; regional earnings are not, so regional affordability ratios use national earnings.

gaps.title: Mortgage interest tax relief (MIRAS) before April 2000
gaps.detail: Relief at source on the first £30,000 of mortgage interest was available until April 2000 and is not modelled, so pre-2000 repayment-mortgage costs are overstated relative to what many borrowers actually paid.
